statement: Relative employment index of ages 22-25 in the most AI-exposed occupation quintile falls >= 5 pts from its 2026 level (Stanford Digital Economy Lab 'Canaries' series, last 2027 release)
status_at_phase_end: The Canaries series first appeared in Aug 2025 (13% relative decline for ages 22-25 in the most-exposed occupations, firm-time controlled, data to Jul 2025), revised in Nov 2025 to 16% (data to Sep 2025); levels: -6% for 22-25 in the most-exposed occupations since late 2022 vs +6-9% for older workers. Pre-2026 vintages, so no 2026 baseline yet; the trend was widening. A broader occupational-mix study (Oct 2025) found no economy-wide disruption.

items.summary: First release of the Canaries series: with payroll data to July 2025, early-career workers (22-25) in the most AI-exposed occupations had a 13% relative employment decline vs the least-exposed, after firm-level controls; older workers in the same occupations were stable or growing.
items.detail: Brynjolfsson, Chandar, Chen, 'Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts...', Stanford Digital Economy Lab working paper, initially circulated August 2025 (day per press coverage, 2025-08-26), ADP data (Bloc A). The Aug-2026 revision confirms the 13% figure for the July-2025 vintage.

items.summary: A policy research lab measuring the occupational mix found no discernible economy-wide labour-market disruption in the 33 months after the first mass-market chatbot launched; exposure, automation and augmentation measures were unrelated to employment changes, though it flagged a possible early-career divergence among recent graduates.
items.detail: The Budget Lab at Yale (with Brookings), 'Evaluating the Impact of AI on the Labor Market: Current State of Affairs', 2025-10-01 (Bloc A).

items.summary: Revised Canaries paper (data to September 2025): relative decline for ages 22-25 in the most-exposed occupations widened to 16% (firm-time controlled; 15 log points top vs bottom quintile). In levels, 22-25-year-olds in the most-exposed occupations were down 6% since late 2022 while older workers were up 6-9%.
items.detail: Canaries November 13, 2025 version PDF (Stanford Digital Economy Lab). Declines concentrated where AI automates (per Anthropic usage data), not augments.
items.value: -16% relative (Sep 2025 data); -15 log pts Q5 vs Q1

items.summary: The authors caution that the patterns are descriptive and may partly reflect other factors (e.g. interest rates, pre-trends); the series is drawn from one payroll processor's clients and covers Bloc A only.
items.detail: Canaries Nov 2025 PDF conclusion: 'our main estimates may be influenced by factors other than generative AI'. ADP sample (Bloc A).

items.summary: The indicator's baseline is the 2026 level, which did not exist in 2025; in 2025 the series existed only as two paper vintages with differing methods, not a regular release. No comparable age-by-exposure series exists for Bloc B.
items.detail: Regular monthly Canaries Dashboard launched only in June 2026. No Bloc B NBS equivalent.
